subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Starbucks: The Second Wave
description: A 60-second lesson on Starbucks: The Second Wave.

hook.text: Starbucks opened in Seattle in 1971 as a bean retailer. It didn't serve brewed coffee for its first 16 years.

buildup.text: Howard Schultz visited Milan in 1983, fell in love with Italian espresso bars, and reimagined Starbucks as a café.

discovery.text: Schultz introduced the concept of the 'third place'—a social space between home and work. It resonated instantly.

twist.text: Today, Starbucks has 35,000+ stores in 80 countries. It normalized $4 coffee and taught Americans the word 'latte.'

climax.text: Critics say Starbucks homogenized café culture. Supporters say it made quality coffee accessible to millions for the first time.

punchline.text: Love it or critique it, Starbucks made coffee culture mainstream.

quiz.question: What concept did Howard Schultz bring to Starbucks from Italy?
options: The 'third place'—a social space between home and work

details.summary: Starbucks, founded in Seattle in 1971, grew from a single store selling whole beans into a global chain with over 35,000 locations. It introduced millions to espresso drinks, created a new language for ordering coffee, and established the cafe as a third place between home and work.
details.whyItMatters: Starbucks transformed coffee from a commodity to a lifestyle product. Love it or critique it, the company fundamentally changed how the world drinks and thinks about coffee.
takeaways: Starbucks grew from one Seattle store to 35,000+ worldwide
It popularized espresso-based drinks for mainstream consumers
It established the cafe as a third place between home and work

faq.question: What was coffee culture like before Starbucks?
faq.answer: Most Americans drank commodity drip coffee at home or at diners. Espresso was rare outside Italian-American neighborhoods. Coffee was a basic caffeinated beverage, not an experience. Starbucks introduced lattes, cappuccinos, and the idea of paying several dollars for a coffee drink.

faq.question: What is the third place concept that Starbucks popularized?
faq.answer: Sociologist Ray Oldenburg coined the term third place for social spaces distinct from home and work. Starbucks deliberately designed stores as comfortable gathering places with seating, music, and wifi. This concept drove the company's real estate and design strategy.
